subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation - post-call follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acmepayments.com>
Cc: Alice Chen <alice.chen@acmepayments.com>
Date: 2026-07-15T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation - quick recap and next steps

Hi John / Alice,

Thanks again for the time today — really helpful to see your production requirements. Short recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment:  

Summary of requirements (as discussed):
- Target SLO: 95th percentile latency <= 200ms for 256-token responses (streaming enabled).
- Peak concurrency: ~40 concurrent user streams.
- Sustained throughput: ~2,500–3,000 tokens/sec during business hours; ~5k tokens/sec burst.
- Response size: median 120 tokens, 95th 320 tokens.
- Model: open-weights LLM variant (ACME-tuned) — you'll provide a quantized ONNX/XT model or we can evaluate using our A/B model variants.
- Hard constraints: data residency in us-west, SOC2 evidence required before go-live.

Attachments: please share a representative sample of traffic (jsonl) and any latency target spreadsheet — I attached our perf validation checklist as well.

Next steps we propose:
1) You confirm sample traffic + any rate shape (attached acme_sample_traffic.jsonl)
2) We run a dedicated capacity validation using your traffic shape — target window: 24–48h run to capture warm cache behavior
3) Internal sizing: Aditya / Rafael to recommend GPU types and reserved throughput to meet the SLO with redundancy
4) Schedule a 60–90m working session to review results and finalize committed capacity + price.

Can you confirm you can share the sample traffic by end of day tomorrow? If yes, we'll queue a perf run the following week.

Thanks,

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-16T11:50:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated capacity performance validation - Acme traffic and targets (for sizing)

Marissa — reviewed the sample traffic and targets. High-level recommendations below (we can refine after a 6–12h synthetic run):

Assumptions and notes:
- Model: ACME-tuned ~13B-ish FP16 / quantized variant. We benchmarked similar models on H100 and A100.
- Streaming increases per-request open socket time but reduces perceived latency; it slightly lowers throughput due to more frequent small writes. We'll use continuous batching + early-token flush to approximate production.

Sizing suggestions (to hit 95p <= 200ms for 256-token streaming responses):
Option A (preferred, lower headroom):
- 3x NVIDIA H100 (full nodes), reserved 24/7, configured with 2 inference workers per GPU
- Reserved throughput: 80 rps sustained (assuming average 120 tokens/response), burst headroom to 160 rps across cluster.
- Expected 95p latency: ~150–190ms (depends on prompt complexity and model variant)

Option B (cost‑savings, more cards):
- 6x NVIDIA A100 80GB, reserved 24/7, 1.5 inference workers per GPU equivalent
- Reserved throughput: 70 rps sustained, burst to 140 rps
- Expected 95p latency: ~170–220ms

If they need 99p <= 250ms, both configs are likely OK with additional auto-burst capacity or an extra H100 (i.e., 4x H100) to provide safety for promotional spikes. For the 60-concurrency spikes, recommend enabling burst pool (dedicated burst capacity) to avoid QoS degradation.

Streaming considerations:
- Enable per-connection early-token flush and a smaller per-batch token limit; this slightly increases CPU/network load but preserves perceived latency.
- KV prefix caching: if they have session prefixes / repeated prompts, caching will reduce token-level work significantly; we should request a cacheable subset of prompts.

Perf run plan:
- 24h run: baseline steady-state at sustained traffic + 3x 15-minute promotional spikes to 6k tokens/sec to observe behavior.
- Deliverables: latency percentiles (P50/P95/P99), token throughput, GPU utilization, and end-to-end streaming RTT breakdown.
- Estimated runtime to produce a validated sizing doc: 2 business days after run completes.

I'll schedule the synthetic run once Marissa confirms the sample traffic is final. Rafael — can you confirm whether 3x H100 fits within our Dedicated capacity pool for an early August start?

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Staff ML Engineer, Inference
aditya@redwood.com

Subject: Proposed dedicated sizing and next steps (RDW-4982)

John / Alice — thanks for sending the sample payloads. Internal sizing proposal below so we can align on budget and schedule the perf validation.

Proposed initial committed config (recommended):
- 3x NVIDIA H100 nodes (reserved Dedicated capacity, us-west)
- Reserved throughput: baseline 80 rps (sustained), burst pool to 160 rps across cluster
- Streaming: enabled with early-token flush; we'll tune batching to keep P95 <= 200ms
- Validation plan: 24h perf run (sustained + 3x bursts) -> detailed report and recommended final committed capacity within 2 business days after run.

Alternative (cost-conscious) option: 6x A100 nodes with slightly higher latency headroom.

Open items / asks from Acme:
- Confirm you shared acme_sample_traffic.jsonl and the latency spreadsheet (got both).
- Confirm target window for the perf run (we can start as early as Mon Aug 3 if you approve).

- Confirm any regulatory constraints for US-West (we will ensure SOC2 evidence collection in parallel).
- Point person for day-of-run alerting (who should we ping if we see QoS issues?).

If this looks good I will: 1) schedule the perf run, 2) lock the preliminary quote into the deal, and 3) kick off SSO/SOC2 touchpoints with Alice.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call to walk through the plan.

Best,
